The notebook nonetheless calls it 'on the tail tip'. The accuracy numbers suggest the tail is missing. Without the tail, the expected value is E064/65's pool 0.7552 minus ~0.08 pp for a 0.25 ep 24 px trim, about 0.7544, and E070 scored 0.7542. With the tail, adding the tail (+0.25), the schedule (+0.12) and the trim (−0.08) predicts ~0.757–0.758, which is 0.3 pp above what was observed. In both readings the current tip is a single run, and seed 2 sits at 0.7502.

critiques.target: H4 pooling rule as applied (E066, E067, E063)

It scored 0.7570 but was excluded as 'noise-high', while low draws of math-neutral variants stayed in the family. E067 was bit-identical per seed to E062 and still enters the tip pool as an independent sample, which breaks the H4 rule's 'non-bit-identical' requirement. The tip pool has been quoted as 0.7531, 0.7533, 0.7537, 0.7538 and 0.7540 depending on membership. With E066 included and E067 dropped, the E062-code family is ~0.7550. Against that, the tail's pool of 0.7562 is +0.12 pp, not +0.25.
critiques.suggestion: Write one membership rule: every same-math, non-bit-identical run, regardless of sign. Recompute every 'supports' verdict since E057 under that rule. Record bit-identical reruns as a single sample.

critiques.issue: The evidence is two runs: 0.7579, which is above the preregistered upper bound, and 0.7544, which falls inside the old family range. That is a +0.25 pp claim at roughly 1.8 SE against a cherry-picked baseline (see above). Since E057 the loop has tested about 7 zero-cost levers: floor, warmup, whitening-bias freeze, head LR, Inductor flags, tail and schedule. At ~1.5–2 SE thresholds, one or two false positives are expected. The tail also changes four things at once (floor hold, lookahead stop, final EMA, eval on EMA with net BN buffers), so even a real gain cannot be attributed to any one of them.

critiques.target: E065 → E070 planning arithmetic ('buys accuracy at 0.13 pp per 1%')
critiques.issue: The 'net opportunity' plan stacks three noisy estimates: E064/65 vs the tip pool (+0.12 pp, 2 vs 2 runs, SE of the difference ~0.15), the 0.03–0.04 pp per 1% trim slope (single runs against lucky references, as H2.10 itself admits), and the tail's +0.25. critiques.target: H2 Lvl1 / H2.10 (32 px tail as the untested biggest reservoir)
critiques.issue: The 32 px phase is ~71% of time. Yet on the current Muon/tail base, no fractional trim of the 32 px tail (e.g. 3.75@32) has been run. The claim that the '32 px tail is binding' rests on E025, a single run with an ambiguous base. E025's description says eager Muon, but its 0.73 s saving versus E021 only fits if it ran on the compiled-Muon E024 base. H2.10.2's arm B, the one direct test, was retired without running.
critiques.suggestion: After the provenance and margin checks, run 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 3.75@32 and compare it at equal time against a further 24 px trim. Every 24 px step removed so far erodes the bridge that E032 showed matters, and 32 px trims may trade comparably.

critiques.target: H2.15 / H2.15.1 (whitening-bias freeze as a FLOP lever)
critiques.issue: E061 froze the bias only by setting its LR to 0, so requires_grad stayed on and the group-1 conv1 dgrad was still computed. The time change (−0.3%) is noise and tests nothing. E061 did show that the freeze costs nothing in accuracy (−0.08 pp, closed), which is exactly the precondition for the FLOP version. Yet the evidence was filed under H8.1, and H2.15.1 remains unrun.
critiques.suggestion: Run H2.15.1 as specified: requires_grad=False after 20% of steps, separate static graphs keyed by bias-grad, both warmed up in build. Confirm in the compiled backward graph that the dgrad is gone. It is a math-neutral time lever, which is the only kind the current margin can bank safely.

critiques.target: H4.4 / H4.5 (bit-identical reruns are unexplained evidence)
critiques.issue: Two rerun pairs came out bit-identical (E044/E045, E062/E067), while other reruns of the same code diverged by 0.1–0.6 pp per seed. That fits a discrete mixture over per-process cuDNN algorithm pick sets with near-tied benchmarks. It supports H4.5 but is not logged as evidence. E067 was supposed to log kernel names per layer (H4.5.1), but no result is reported. No Lvl1 accounts for why per-seed spread varies so much between runs: E063 spans 0.7543–0.7548, E070 spans 0.7502–0.7571.
critiques.suggestion: Report the kernel-name sets from E067 onward and attach E045/E067 as H4.5 evidence. If a pick set predicts a run's mean offset, then restricting picks in build (without deterministic=True) becomes an accuracy lever that also reduces decision noise.

structured_output.summary:
The loop's engineering work is solid and reproducible: static shapes (−2.0%), the max pool fix (−2.9%), the prepare cuts (−0.9%), compiled Muon and bs 1536 are all real. The accuracy side is weaker. Every 'supports' verdict since E057 (head LR 0.5x, the Fable tail, the 2@16+1.5@24 reshuffle) rests on 2-run pools at about 1–2 SE. The baseline those pools are compared against shifts with membership choices: high E066 (0.7570) was left out, bit-identical E067 was counted as independent, and the head-LR bar was passed by rounding. Across ~7 zero-cost tries, one or two false positives are expected.

The most urgent issue is the provenance of the current tip, E070. Its description puts it on E064 code, which predates the tail, but the notebook calls it the 'tail tip'. Its accuracy (0.7542) matches the no-tail prediction almost exactly and sits ~0.3 pp below the with-tail prediction. So either a free +0.2 pp is sitting unused, or the tail and the reshuffle do not stack.

Recommended next steps, in order:
1. Diff the hashes to settle E070's base.
2. Run an untimed seeds 3-10 margin check on the real tip; nothing accuracy-changing has had one since E048.
3. Adopt off-seed runs as the A/B instrument for zero-cost levers.
4. Spend remaining effort on math-neutral time levers, chiefly the real requires_grad whitening freeze (E061 never tested the FLOP saving), and on an untested fractional trim of the 32 px tail, which is 71% of time.

The Lvl1 statements of H2 and H6 are stale. None of the Lvl1 claims explain the bit-identical-vs-divergent rerun pattern or the wide variation in per-seed spread between runs.
